label: Copy-phase steps in long sequences (L>=8), early recall (2-4) or final recall (7-8)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, never on original tokens or <DEL>, and almost only when L>=8 (L=9 holds 81% of mass, L<=6 is essentially zero). Within those sequences it is position-locked to two windows: recall_idx 2-4 (t=11-13, peak at recall 3) and the last recalled tokens 7-8 (t=16-17). Mass is highest at recall_idx 3 and at the final step of L=9 sequences. The predicate covers about 94% of activation mass but has low precision (about 8%): only a small fraction of the matching steps actually fire. Firing at those positions depends on token identity in a way no simple rule captures. Some input tokens (b, 2, y, g, 1, j) give 3-4x lift, and more digits in the sequence raises the rate. Hand-picked token lists raise F1 only to about 0.3, so the token dependence is left unexplained. Magnitudes are small overall (max about 0.011).
